newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX ends bourse session above 2,900 level.
newsitem.headline: German DAX ends bourse session above 2,900 level.

text.p: The German DAX index, powered by a surge in German bonds, on Thursday closed floor trading above 2,900 for the first time.

The blue-chip index soared 43.84 points in bourse dealings to close at 2,909.91, surprising experts who had predicted profit-taking would hold off another run at the magical 2,900 mark for at least another several trading sessions.
After climbing to an all-time high of 2,914.61 by 1100 GMT, the bourse DAX settled to around 2,909.00 losing momentum after the Bundesbank said key interest rates would remain unchanged.
A rally in German Bunds, spurred by a rise in unemployment, sparked the stock rise. Bunds rose as much as 30 basis points before tumbling after the Bundesbankleft left rates untouched.
Bunds climbed as the unemployment figures had lifted hopes the central bank would ease its stance against rate cuts.

Germany added 50,000 to seasonally adjusted unemployment rolls in November, lifting the total number to 4.1 million. The adjusted joblessness rate rose to 10.7 percent, up from 10.1 percent in October.
Traders had been ready for a restrained bourse session after two days of Wall Street setbacks, and questioned whether the DAX could maintain its lofty level.
"I am skeptical. We need a consolidation. I must warn that it's not institutional investors who are leading this rally," said one Frankfurt trader.

Among shares on the plus side, industrial group Mannesmann AG climbed 25.5 marks, or four percent, to 685 marks on rumours of a merger between its telecommunications unit and that of German utility Veba AG.
Mannesmann officials said they had no information that could explain the rise.

Car makers BMW AG and Volkswagen AG also surged, as both saw increases in November car sales in Japan. BMW, whose November sales in Japan climbed 41.5 percent, rallied 31 marks on the bourse to 1,079 marks by 1015 GMT.

Volkswagen climbed four marks on the bourse to 602.5 marks, following a more than six mark jump in morning IBIS trading. VW's Japan sales rose 16.1 percent in November, although its Audi luxury unit saw a 5.5 percent drop.
